title: The Antikythera Mechanism: An Ancient Computer
question: How did a shipwrecked bronze device from 2,000 years ago encode astronomical calculations so precise that nothing comparable was built again for over a millennium?
summary: Recovered from a Roman-era shipwreck in 1901, the Antikythera mechanism turned out to be a geared analog computer that modeled the motions of the sun, moon, and planets and predicted eclipses — a level of mechanical sophistication historians assumed didn't exist until the medieval astronomical clock, a thousand years later.
